parts.text:
The workspace is essentially empty except for .git and .opencode. Java 26 and Maven 3.10.0 are available. Let me set up a Maven Spring Boot project.

Spring Boot 3.x requires Java 17+. Java 26 is very new. Let me use a recent Spring Boot version. Spring Boot 3.4.x or 3.5.x. Let me check what's available. I'll use Spring Boot 3.5.x which should work.

Let me create the project structure. I'll set up:
- pom.xml
- src/main/java/com/example/demo/DemoApplication.java
- src/main/java/com/example/demo/controller/HelloController.java
- src/main/resources/application.properties
- src/test/java/com/example/demo/DemoApplicationTests.java
- .gitignore

Let me plan with a todo list since this is multi-step. Actually it's straightforward but a handful of files. Let me create them.

Let me pick Spring Boot version 3.5.4 (as of the date). Actually today's date is Oct 2026, so Spring Boot 3.5.x is fine. But Java 26 compatibility might be an issue with older Spring Boot. Spring Boot 3.5 supports up to Java 24 maybe. Java 26 may need Spring Boot 4.0. Let me check. Spring Boot 4.0 was released Nov 2025, requiring Java 17+ and supporting Java 25. Hmm.

Actually, to be safe, let me check what Spring Boot versions exist. Let me fetch metadata from Maven Central. But I shouldn't guess URLs unless confident for programming. Maven Central is fine.

Let me just set up with a reasonably current version and verify by building. Let me check network access.

Spring Boot 4.1.1 is the latest stable. Let me check its Java compatibility. Spring Boot 4.0 baseline is Java 17. Let me use 4.1.1. Let me verify the Java version compatibility. Spring Boot 4.x supports Java 17-25? Java 26 might not be officially supported but it may still work. Actually let me check what Java versions Spring Boot 4.1 supports.

Rather than guess, let me set the java.version property. With Java 26 installed, I can target release 21 for compatibility, which any Spring Boot 4.x supports. That's safe. Let me use Java 21 as the target.

Actually, let me set java.version to 21. The maven compiler will need to support --release 21, which JDK 26 does.

Let me create the project now.

input.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <parent>
        <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
        <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-parent</artifactId>
        <version>4.1.1</version>
        <relativePath/>
    </parent>

    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
    <artifactId>demo</artifactId>
    <version>0.0.1-SNAPSHOT</version>
    <name>demo</name>
    <description>REST API web application</description>

    <properties>
        <java.version>21</java.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-web</artifactId>
        </dependency>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-validation</artifactId>
        </dependency>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-test</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
                <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

- `src/main/java/com/example/demo/DemoApplication.java` — entry point
- `src/main/java/com/example/demo/controller/GreetingController.java` — sample endpoint at `GET /api/hello?name=...`
- `src/main/resources/application.properties` — app name/port
- `src/test/java/com/example/demo/DemoApplicationTests.java` — context-load test
- `.gitignore`

Run with `mvn spring-boot:run`, test with `mvn test`, package with `mvn package`. Live check returned `{"message":"Hello, Spring!"}`.
